transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place. It's probably not a huge deal compared to what you usually see, but... well, I recently decided to try and turn my art into a real freelance business. Which is a good thing, really! I'm very lucky to be able to try. 

But I guess I keep getting pretty wound up over the business side of things, like invoices and client messages. I get a little overwhelmed and then I end up just... avoiding them, I guess? And then it piles up, and... I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, but I'll end up just crying at my kitchen table about it. Or I get so scattered that I start forgetting normal, everyday stuff, like paying my own bills. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit silly, but... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you can help with?
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of the stress with your freelance work?

Oh, um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I mean, I still really love the actual art part of it, and I still enjoy seeing my friends and doing my normal hobbies. It's really just... just when I have to look at the emails and the invoices that I get all upset. 

Outside of that, I'm usually pretty cheerful! I try to be, anyway. I hope that's a good thing? Like, I'm not feeling down about my whole life or anything, I still have a lot of fun when I'm not stressing over the business stuff. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.

When you get overwhelmed with the business tasks, do you ever experience sudden episodes of intense fear or panic, like your heart racing, feeling short of breath, or like something terrible is going to happen?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say it's like a panic attack or anything that intense. I mean, my heart might beat a little faster just because I'm flustered, but I'm definitely not feeling like I can't breathe or that the world is ending. 

It's more just... a really strong wave of frustration and feeling inadequate, I guess. I just get worked up and have a little cry, but I don't feel terrified. I hope that's okay? Like, I don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is. I'm just a bit of a worrier when it comes to the paperwork, that's all. Is that a normal way to react to stress?

Outside of the stress related to your freelance business tasks, have you noticed any other areas in your life where you feel your emotions or reactions are causing significant difficulties or impairments?

Well, um... I guess it is spilling over just a tiny bit into other things, but I'm really trying to keep it under control! It's mainly just that the business side takes up so much mental energy. Like, I'll put off replying to a client because I don't know what to say, and then... well, I was so focused on trying to get an art display ready and worrying about the emails that I actually missed a utility payment for the house. 

I know that sounds really irresponsible, and I felt awful about it! I usually always pay my bills on time. It's just that I get so caught up in trying to balance the freelance work and the home stuff, and sometimes things slip through the cracks. But it's not a regular thing, I promise! I'm really trying to do better. Do you think that's understandable, given everything I'm trying to juggle right now?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things other than your freelance business, like everyday events or responsibilities, even when there isn't a clear problem to solve?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I try not to worry too much about everyday things. Like I said, I'm usually pretty cheerful! 

I think... well, I think most of my stress is really just tied to the business side of my art, and trying to keep up with all the emails and invoices. When it comes to normal stuff, like running errands or seeing friends, I don't sit around worrying about it. I mean, sure, everyone worries a little bit sometimes, right? But it's not like I'm constantly anxious about things that aren't actually a problem. I hope that makes sense? I really try to just focus on the positives when I'm not dealing with the freelance paperwork. Is it normal to just have that one main thing that stresses you out?
When you avoid dealing with the business tasks like emails and invoices, is it mainly because starting them feels emotionally overwhelming, even if you know they’re important?

Um, yeah... I think that's exactly it. I know they're important, I really do! I want to be professional and do a good job. But ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, I just keep getting so wound up over the invoices and client messages. 

It just feels so big and scary to start them, so I kind of... push them away. And then I avoid them until, well, until I'm just sitting at my kitchen table having a little cry, or forgetting normal stuff like paying that bill I mentioned earlier. That's honestly why I finally decided to come in and talk to someone. I just want to be able to handle it all better without getting so overwhelmed, you know? I hope it doesn't sound too silly that I let emails get me so worked up... is it okay that I feel that way?
Outside of business tasks like emails and invoices, do you ever have trouble getting started on other things you need to do, even when you know they’re important?

Oh, um... no, not really! I think I'm actually pretty good at getting started on normal things. Like, if the house needs cleaning or I need to run to the grocery store, I just do it. I don't really procrastinate on everyday stuff. 

It's really just the freelance business things that trip me up, like I said. The rest of my life is pretty organized, I promise! I always try to keep on top of my regular chores and everything. I mean, everyone puts off doing the laundry sometimes, right? But it's not a big problem or anything. I'm doing okay with all the normal stuff... does that sound alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
How long have you been feeling this way about the business tasks—has it been going on since you started the freelance work, or did it develop more recently?

Um, let me think... it hasn't been that long, really. I'd say it's been going on for about a month now. That's when I really started trying to shift my art into, you know, a more formal freelance business instead of just a hobby. 

Before that, I was totally fine! I loved just painting and creating without all the pressure. But once I started trying to make it official a few weeks ago, that's when the emails and the invoices started getting to me. So it's pretty recent, I promise I haven't been letting things slide for months and months or anything! I really am trying my best to figure it out quickly. A month isn't too terribly long to be struggling with something new, is it? I hope it's normal to have a little adjustment period like this.
When you're feeling overwhelmed by the business tasks, do you find yourself physically restless, like you can't sit still or you feel tense in your body?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I get physically restless or anything like that. I mean, I might fidget a little bit with my pen if I'm staring at an email I don't want to send, but nothing major! I definitely don't feel like I can't sit still. 

I'm usually pretty calm physically, I promise. It's more just... in my head, you know? Like a mental block where I just feel overwhelmed, rather than my body feeling tense or jittery. I try really hard to stay relaxed, maybe take a deep breath or two. I think I'm doing okay on that front! Is that what you mean, just normal little fidgets? I hope it's okay that I don't feel it in my body like that.
Have you noticed that you feel unusually tired or lacking in energy, even when you haven't been doing anything physically demanding?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I get a little tired sometimes, but who doesn't, right? I definitely don't feel unusually exhausted or anything. 

I'm pretty good at keeping my energy up, I promise! I still have plenty of energy to do my painting and take care of the house. It's just those business tasks that make me feel a little drained, but not in a physical way. I make sure I get enough sleep and everything, so I'm doing really well with that. I hope that's a good thing? I really try not to let myself get too run down.
